about.en:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Chengdu, China, on 28–29 November 2026, hosted by SPGS International School Chengdu. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.

en: Four team events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for a Global Round and the Yale Tournament of Champions

eligibility.en: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; independent teams are welcome. Divisions: Senior (born on or before 1 July 2012) and Junior (younger); scholars must be born on or before 31 December 2016.

en: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Open the WSC registration portal and choose this round (or use the round's Request Info link)
Register the team and any accompanying adults, and pay the fee by card or bank transfer
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum before the round
Attend the round in Chengdu, 28–29 November 2026

costs.en: Registration fee per scholar (student): regular 868 CNY. Adults/coaches register separately; travel, accommodation and most meals are extra. Payment by card or bank transfer through the WSC portal.

about.en:
Global Rounds are the second stage of the World Scholar's Cup: teams that qualified at a regional round meet scholars from many countries for several days of Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge and the Scholar's Bowl, plus the Scholar's Show, cultural fair and Scholar's Ball. The Tokyo-Yokohama Mini Global Round runs 11–15 December 2026 with Pacifico Yokohama as the main venue; debates are held at nearby schools.

about.en:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Perth, Australia, on 4–5 June 2027, hosted by Sacred Heart College. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.

en: Four team events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for a Global Round and the Yale Tournament of Champions

eligibility.en: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; independent teams are welcome. Divisions: Senior (born on or before 1 July 2013) and Junior (younger); scholars must be born on or before 31 December 2016.

en: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Open the WSC registration portal and choose this round (or use the round's Request Info link)
Register the team and any accompanying adults, and pay the fee by card or bank transfer
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum before the round
Attend the round in Perth, 4–5 June 2027

costs.en: Registration fee per scholar (student): regular 120 AUD, late 140 AUD. Adults/coaches register separately; travel, accommodation and most meals are extra. Payment by card or bank transfer through the WSC portal.

about.en:
The Tournament of Champions is the final of the World Scholar's Cup season, hosted with the Yale International Relations Association at Yale University, New Haven, on 12–18 November 2026. Scholars compete again in Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge and the Scholar's Bowl, and also attend a panel on college life and admissions, talks by keynote speakers including a Yale professor, the Yale Ball and a scavenger hunt.

Only qualified teams can attend: all three scholars must have qualified at a 2026 Global Round (or the 2025 Dubai Holiday Special Global Round), with at least two who qualified as teammates, and all participants must be at least 11 years old. Delegation coordinators register qualified teams through the WSC ToC registration portal; visa invitation letters are available on request.

about.en:
Future We Want Model United Nations (FWWMUN) runs international Model UN conferences on five continents. FWWMUN Madrid takes place on 8–11 March 2027 in a partner 4- or 5-star hotel (venue to be confirmed). It opens with expert-led workshops on youth involvement, the Sustainable Development Goals and leadership, followed by committee sessions in which delegates represent countries or NGOs, negotiate and draft resolutions.

High-school delegates (ages 13–19) and university delegates (ages 17–26) from any country can register as individuals or as a delegation; high-school delegations must bring a faculty advisor. No prior MUN experience is required: first-timers are placed in introductory committees and experienced delegates in advanced ones. Country/NGO assignments are released in rounds, background guides are provided, and position papers are due a few weeks before the event.

Registration is first come, first served (regular registration is open); late registration opens 28 December 2026 and all conference fees are due by 31 January 2027. Financial-aid (scholarship) applications open during the cycle, and invitation letters for visas are issued after payment. It suits students who want a large, international MUN experience abroad focused on UN diplomacy.

en: International delegates from many countries; individual or delegation registration
Opening workshops with diplomats and experts on the SDGs, youth involvement and leadership
Financial-aid applications available during the registration cycle

eligibility.en: High-school students aged 13–19 and university students aged 17–26 who are currently enrolled, from any country. Individuals may register alone; high-school delegations need at least one faculty advisor. English is the working language; no prior MUN experience needed.

en: Open the FWWMUN Madrid page and read Registration & Costs and Terms & Conditions
Register as a delegate (or observer) individually or as a delegation
Apply for financial aid during the scholarship window if needed
Pay all conference fees by 31 January 2027 and book the partner hotel package if wanted
Request a visa invitation letter after payment if required
Receive your country/NGO assignment and submit the position paper by 17 February 2027

costs.en: Conference fee per participant (Basic conference-only package or packages with partner-hotel accommodation, prices shown in the FWW registration system); optional Certified Training USD 49. Flights, visas and meals outside the package are extra. Partial financial aid can be requested.

score_reason: Large international MUN brand with published key dates and open registration; costly once travel is added.

about.en:
The International History Bee and Bowl (IHBB), run by International Academic Competitions, is a buzzer-based history quiz for school students. The History Bowl is a team event (up to a full school team, with 2-person and solo options) and the History Bee is an individual event; questions cover world history, geography and culture. The 2026 Fall History Bee and Bowl of London takes place at City of London School, London, on 22 November 2026.

Students compete in age divisions (Varsity, Junior Varsity, Middle School and Elementary, by date of birth). Students can also sit the Science Bee and Geography Bee qualifying exams during the lunch break. Top students and teams qualify for the 2027 IHBB European Championships and world-level IAC events such as the International History Olympiad. It is a good first international competition for students who love history and quizzes.

about.en:
The International History Bee and Bowl (IHBB), run by International Academic Competitions, is a buzzer-based history quiz for school students. The History Bowl is a team event (up to a full school team, with 2-person and solo options) and the History Bee is an individual event; questions cover world history, geography and culture. The 2027 History Bee and Bowl of Paris takes place at École Jeannine Manuel, Paris, on 30 January 2027.

Students compete in age divisions (Varsity, Junior Varsity, Middle School and Elementary, by date of birth). Students can also sit the Science Bee and Geography Bee qualifying exams during the lunch break. Top students and teams qualify for the 2027 IHBB European Championships and world-level IAC events such as the International History Olympiad. It is a good first international competition for students who love history and quizzes.
